reason: Mixed case: the core addition tests use listed operators, nil lifting, XML templates, constants/type definitions, listed langlib subtype names and supported method calls. However, the executable wrapper imports ballerina/io and invokes io:println, which is outside the spec's exclusive supported-library list. This makes the whole source a feature case under the requested any-unsupported-construct rule.
unsupported_constructs: import ballerina/io and io:println calls in main (library absent from the exclusive supported list)
test_design_notes: Supported addition coverage and unsupported output scaffolding are mixed in one source; isolating the wrapper would allow separate assessment of the addition behavior.
All named test functions are called from main; assertion failures panic. No obvious omitted invocation or malformed output marker is visible in the supplied source.

The nullable side-effect test relies on the initial module variable intVal = 10 and main invokes it before the nonnullable test resets intVal; the visible call order is consistent with its assertions.
